chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Hi, I'm Charlotte and I'm here to talk about artificial intelligence.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Did you know there are five big ideas in AI?

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: They are perception, representation and reasoning,

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: learning from data, natural interaction, and societal impact.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Number one is perception.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Perception is when a computer uses sensors to gather data,

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: and then extracts meaning from those signals.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Number two, representation and reasoning.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Representation is when a computer builds its own world so that it can understand,

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: just like a Google map.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: That's an example of a representation of how the computer perceives the world.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Then it can apply reasoning to that representation.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: For example, to take you on the correct bike path or to route you via Uber.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Number three, learning from data.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Computers use a lot of data to do the processing that allows them to think artificially.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: That's artificial intelligence.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Almost all AI systems are made from a lot, a lot of data.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Number four, natural interaction.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Natural interaction is when we've trained an AI system to interact naturally with the people around it.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: That means that you can trust Google Translate to say the words that you're saying in another language,

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: or perhaps you use facial recognition and you trust that that system will only let the correct people into the building.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Number five, societal impact.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: AI affects our world in positive and negative ways.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: AI makes it so that no one in the world starves.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: But we also have to make sure to guard against implicit bias

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: and make sure that the computer algorithms that we write are fair for everyone.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: So these are the five big ideas in AI.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Perception, representation and reasoning, learning from data, natural interaction and societal impact.

chunks.title: 5 Big Ideas about AI
chunks.text: Watch more videos to learn more in depth about each of these ideas.

text: Hi, I'm Charlotte and I'm here to talk about artificial intelligence. Did you know there are five big ideas in AI? They are perception, representation and reasoning, learning from data, natural interaction, and societal impact. Number one is perception. Perception is when a computer uses sensors to gather data, and then extracts meaning from those signals. Number two, representation and reasoning. Representation is when a computer builds its own world so that it can understand, just like a Google map. That's an example of a representation of how the computer perceives the world. Then it can apply reasoning to that representation. For example, to take you on the correct bike path or to route you via Uber. Number three, learning from data. Computers use a lot of data to do the processing that allows them to think artificially. That's artificial intelligence. Almost all AI systems are made from a lot, a lot of data. Number four, natural interaction. Natural interaction is when we've trained an AI system to interact naturally with the people around it. That means that you can trust Google Translate to say the words that you're saying in another language, or perhaps you use facial recognition and you trust that that system will only let the correct people into the building. Number five, societal impact. AI affects our world in positive and negative ways. AI makes it so that no one in the world starves. But we also have to make sure to guard against implicit bias and make sure that the computer algorithms that we write are fair for everyone. So these are the five big ideas in AI. Perception, representation and reasoning, learning from data, natural interaction and societal impact. Watch more videos to learn more in depth about each of these ideas.
